All five bodies and all 29 original displayed equations are byte-identical.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every regular energy for a real simply characteristic p without invariant directions and rough symmetric short-range V; arbitrary noncompact or empty shells, unbounded g, both labels and full Xp.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The energy extension has density b/g. Threshold bounds control every derivative-of-p multiplier divided by g, so each graph component is the bounded surface extension of an L2 density. Conversely the homogeneous classification applies to each graph component; summing the n gradient norms gives ||gv||2<=C||u||Xp. This gives an isomorphism with unweighted amplitudes without assuming g bounded above. Applying the forced theorem to -Vu gives unique opposite-boundary homogeneous additions; its jump yields bplus-bminus=-2pi i TVu. Extended symmetry makes the flux imaginary part zero. Dividing surface densities by g yields exact equality of the two physical norms, both finite since 1/g is bounded. Empty shells give zero homogeneous space.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every good energy and every B forcing, paired with every stationary Xp solution; exact unitary Fourier normalization and linear-first convention.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The canonical transform is the trace of the inverted B forcing h. Extension duality with b/g gives the physical pairing as (h,uplus/minus). Inserting the opposite-boundary addition and conjugate free boundary adjointness moves R0 to h with the matching sign. Extended V symmetry moves V and the inverted forcing identity gives (f,u). All pairings are B/Bstar pairings and are finite. Free adjointness follows from nonreal adjointness and weak-star limits against fixed B elements, so no unproved trace of an ambient representative or extra Fourier constant is used.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: All regular energies, including point spectrum; exact entire L2 eigenspace, finite dimension, rapid decay and actual closed operator domain; general Banach Xp.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Aplus kernel gives one zero amplitude, flux gives the other, proving equal kernels. The earlier rapid/domain theorem puts them in D(H), and the whole-eigenfunction theorem supplies the converse. Bounded free boundary after compact V makes R0V compact; the general Banach Fredholm proof gives closed range and index zero. V is injective on the kernel by the boundary equation. Opposite-boundary adjointness and V symmetry annihilate the range against every Vw. These r functionals are independent by compact smooth testing and V injectivity. Their joint kernel has codimension r by finite-dimensional linear algebra, so containment and equality of codimension give the exact range. No representation of the full Banach dual by B functions is assumed.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every unweighted L2 incoming or outgoing amplitude at any regular energy, including eigenvalues; a bounded linear range solver chosen on a closed complement.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For each kernel vector the two free boundaries agree, so the injective jump/zero-trace criterion gives TVw=0. Extension duality annihilates the free incoming wave against Vw, giving exact Fredholm solvability. Two solutions differ in the common kernel and hence have identical outgoing amplitudes. Reversing signs gives the inverse amplitude map. Continuous finite-dimensional coordinates and Hahn-Banach extensions give a bounded kernel projection. On its closed complement, a failed inverse norm bound would yield unit yj with Ayj->0 and compact Cyj convergent, hence a unit vector in the zero intersection. This proves the bounded range solver. The difference S-I=-2pi i TVGE factors through compact V and bounded maps, so is compact; the reverse solver bounds S inverse. All signs follow the unchanged opposite-boundary amplitude labels.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every exponent kappa from zero through two, with compatible compact extensions and inverse on each space, physical unitarity at one; weight may approach zero.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The weight a=1/g is positive bounded continuous on the regular shell, with no required positive infimum. Unweighted S-I is compact and the flux identity gives ||Sb||a=||b||a on the unweighted dense domain. Every hypothesis of the complete U017 theorem is therefore met; its weighted adjoint, compatible second endpoint, cutoff compactness and three-lines proof give exactly the whole closed interval of exponents and unitarity in the middle. Empty shells are zero spaces. No norm continuity in energy or stronger decay assumption is added.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every momentum L2 input, physical weighted fiber action at almost every energy; canonical B traces at every good energy, no prior measurable operator-field assumption.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The two exact stationary pairings show (Jplus f,Sb)=(Jminus f,b). Unitarity and explicit density via 1_{g<=N}h give Jplus f=S Jminus f at every good energy. Onto Jminus and dense B give global approximants with summable L2 errors, and Q unitarity gives the same for outputs. Coarea and scalar L2 triangle bound every partial sum of fiber error norms; monotone convergence bounds the infinite sum, so both errors tend to zero in fiber norm outside one null set. Countably many canonical representative identifications can share this null set. Fiber unitarity passes the pointwise equality to the limit. Countable Sigma and its polynomial preimage are null. The resulting Qh supplies the measurable representative, while coarea identifies representatives on almost all fibers and proves independence. The claim is not promoted to every-energy evaluation of arbitrary ambient L2 inputs.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Any regular-energy bound-state ambiguity, with the explicit one-dimensional negative-energy example and zero amplitude spaces.

The earlier exact H2 example H=-d2-2sech^2 has actual eigenfunction sech at -1. This energy is regular for the free square, with empty real shell. Its nonzero eigenkernel coexists with the unique identity on zero amplitude space, so no uniqueness of the interior stationary solution is falsely inferred.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every L2 sphere amplitude, exact unitary Fourier convention at d3,lambda1,g2; actual graph-space averaged solution and smooth bounded kernel.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The free energy extension has coefficient1/[2(2pi)^(3/2)]. Finite sphere area makes each L2 amplitude L1. The continuous bounded C(ball)-valued solution family times b is strongly measurable and norm integrable; the Banach integral allows bounded inverse and point evaluations through. Scalar Fubini for compact spatial convolution uses locally integrable1/r and uniform solution bounds. Thus the average has the same integral equation, free term in Xp and bounded compact forcing in B; R0+ supplies the remaining Xp term. Applying the exact amplitude jump gives kernel -i kappa J/(8pi^2). Constant1/sqrt2 conversion to the usual sphere Hilbert norm leaves the kernel unchanged. The elementary difference-of-squares identity gives |r omega-y|=r-omega.y+O(1/r) uniformly for |y|<=1, and reciprocal/phase bounds give G=e^ir e^-iomega.y/(4pi r)+O(r^-2). Integrating proves outgoing amplitude -kappa J/(4pi), consistent with the stated normalization. These steps avoid integrating individual plane waves as Xp-valued objects.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Explicit compact smooth potential satisfying all rho4 derivative bounds in d3, actual smooth kernel and positive lower bound on off-diagonal neighborhoods.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Exponential difference <=|omega-omegaprime| on the unit ball and the uniform1/7 solution error give |J-Iw|<=Iw(1/7+delta). For0<delta<=1/7, |J|>=5Iw/7 and hence |k|>=5kappa Iw/(56pi^2). The global bound ||psi||<=8/7 gives |k|<=kappa Iw/(7pi^2); compact integration with the proved incident derivatives gives smoothness in both directions. Any putative C delta bound contradicts the lower bound on a nonempty open set of pairs with delta sufficiently small. Positive chart Jacobians give that set positive product measure, so changing a representative on a null set cannot fix the inequality. No general substitute decay-exponent theorem is asserted.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Arbitrary physical shell Hilbert space; spectrum on unit circle, finite multiplicity and no accumulation away from one; unrestricted multiplicity at one.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For V0, S=I; disjoint positive-measure spherical annuli give infinitely many orthogonal eigenvectors at one. Neumann series invert S-s outside the unit circle, using S inverse=S* inside it. For s different from one, identity plus scaled compact factor and the compact alternative show every noninvertible value is an eigenvalue. On that eigenspace K=(s-1)I, so infinite orthonormal sequences contradict compactness. Unitarity makes distinct eigenvectors orthogonal. Infinitely many distinct eigenvalues bounded away from one would give pairwise separated compact images of normalized eigenvectors, impossible. The order epsilon,R,delta,then h is retained.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: The frozen scalar glancing normal block, all primitive inputs u and hD_xu with L2 residual, homogeneous Dirichlet or unrestricted initial trace, and absorbed bounded lower matrix perturbations.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The companion matrix acts on (u,hD_xu) to give the exact residual(0,Q_hu), with no derivative of the frozen scalar a. At glancing its nilpotent square vanishes, and the perturbation operator norm equals |a| in the Euclidean product norm. Apply (N12) to obtain (N15) with both boundary components and both interior norms. Under the homogeneous Dirichlet condition only the first boundary component vanishes; lower terms remain in the perturbation bound.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Uniformly bounded scalar symbol derivatives with parameters, general bounded two-position amplitudes, and every fixed finite matrix size; cutoffs fixed before taking h small.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The exact eta=h*xi substitution turns a semiclassical left symbol into b(y,h*xi), with frequency derivative gains h^|beta|. The complete packet norm theorem at R=1/h gives M+C_b h. The bounded-amplitude theorem gives both uniform and O(h) amplitude norms. Applying entries to a finite matrix and Cauchy-Schwarz yields the stated s times maximal entry bound, with no false sharp matrix leading norm. Scalar0<=q<=1 acting componentwise has norm at most2 for sufficiently small h, accounting for its fixed derivative constants.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Compact smooth phase cutoff q and symbols with all derivatives of at most polynomial frequency growth, uniform in y, compact normal intervals and0<h<=1; scalar and finite matrix ordered products.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Insert the two kernels and integrate the compact intermediate variable to obtain the exact product integral (N19). The partial transform is exp(i*y*theta)*qhat(theta,eta), rapidly decreasing in theta with every derivative and compact eta support. Each y derivative costs only a theta power. Taylor expansion in h*theta and Fourier inversion produce the exact ordered coefficients(h/i)^alpha. Polynomial growth and arbitrary theta decay bound all derivatives of the integral remainder uniformly, including normal derivatives, with compact eta support. The tangential norm bound controls the remainder operator. If b vanishes near support q, every finite term vanishes and arbitrary J gives O(h^J), retaining frequency tails and matrix multiplication order.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Finite matrix differential A_h of arbitrary fixed order with uniform coefficient bounds, compact scalar Q_h independent of normal x, and distributional L2 solutions W,F without any pre-existing trace of W.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Differentiating the output kernel gives the exact A_h Q_h amplitude. Transposing input derivatives gives the Q_h A_h amplitude with (-hD_z)^beta and the correct positive eta factors. Both are bounded by the two-position amplitude theorem, so the compositions have genuine bounded L2 extensions. Positive derivative terms carry h; the remaining scalar-cutoff commutator factors a(z)-a(y) along a segment. Moving z-y onto the frequency derivative gives an explicit h and a compact-frequency bounded amplitude, proving O(h), also after normal derivatives. Schwartz density and distribution pairing identify these extensions. The localized equation then puts hD_x V in L2. Subtract its norm primitive; tests of zero integral are derivatives of compact tests, forcing the difference to be a constant vector. Scalar mollification and norm Lebesgue points identify that equality almost everywhere. The primitive extends continuously to the endpoints and supplies the weak localized trace.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every finite normal matrix block with one real characteristic root at the selected boundary covector, all lower-order differential terms, every epsilon>0 and all distributional L2 inputs in the stated equation.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Choose epsilon0=epsilon/8 and obtain R,delta,C0 from the normal estimate. Continuity gives a fixed neighborhood where each frozen matrix difference is at most delta/(2s), then choose q and chi. The entrywise tangential estimate gives E_h norm at most delta/2+C h; uniform normal derivative bounds give operator norm continuity. The symbol of A_h-kappa-N-E_h vanishes near support q, so its product with Q is O(h^J). Exact expansion yields the positive commutator sign in (N28). Its commutator and tail have norm at most C1 h||W|| on the hR slab. The proved weak trace permits (N12); ||Q||<=2 gives4epsilon0 and the squared forcing estimate gives2C0 C1²h². Choose h0 so the latter is at mostepsilon/2, then enlarge nonnegative integrals to obtain (N26). No shrinking-cutoff derivative bound is assumed uniform: its fixed constants enter h0.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: The actual scalar variable-coefficient wave near any glancing covector, every smooth first- and zero-order term, distributional u,hD_xu,Q_hu inL2 and coordinate-local cutoffs with their explicit forcing.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Boundary normal coordinates remove mixed principal normal/tangential derivatives. Scaling an ordinary second-order differential operator by h² places first-order terms in h times semiclassical derivatives and zero-order terms in the permitted h-dependent scalar coefficient. Forward links identify the separate propagation proof without treating this trace inequality as that theorem.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: The actual scalar formally self-adjoint wave in boundary normal coordinates and half-density coefficients, all smooth formally self-adjoint first- and zero-order terms, bounded coefficient derivatives on a fixed coordinate extension.

Symmetrization retains its zero-order correction in the tangential self-adjoint operator. U=exp(-i integral b/2) has modulus one and d_x U=-h b U/2. B=S* S gives its exact nonnegative square, without assuming positivity of an arbitrary quantization. Expanding all product commutators gives D8 term by term: [d,C]=-ih Cprime, [R,d]=ih Rprime, and the last symmetrized derivative appears with the minus sign. In particular A=d gives -Rprime.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Real compact smooth tangential q independent of normal position, a fixed normal interval with -partial_x a0>=2c on its support, arbitrary full lower terms from D4, and uniform finite derivative bounds.

For g=(-partial_x a0-c)q²>=0, positive packet compression at width sqrt(h) differs from Op_h(g) by O(h), proving D10 without losing the positive leading coefficient. For D12 choose chi one near support q; Op(chi a) is uniformly bounded, while the complete finite product and tail estimate gives (R-Op(chi a))Q=O(h^J) for every fixed J. For fixed h, output differentiation of Q and the QR differential amplitude yields every tangential Sobolev derivative in L2 for v,d_xv,d_x²v. Even normal mollification preserves oddness; tangential mollification and a fixed normal cutoff give smooth Dirichlet approximants converging with every required derivative. Position truncations converge by inverse-radius derivative bounds and L2 tails. The elementary norm-primitive trace estimate proves trace convergence. Therefore the smooth energy and normal-multiplier identities pass to weak inputs. Differentiating the real form (Rv,v) yields exactly the negative integral sign in D16 and hence D15.

Repeating this operation equals differentiation in R=rho² off zero and provides continuous limits of all proposed derivatives at zero. Integrating those limits from a positive lower endpoint and letting it go to zero proves they are the actual one-sided derivatives. Compact parameter differentiation commutes with the integrals; each k-th derivative uses at most2k rho derivatives and has the stated uniform bound. Choose epsilon_j successively so every finite mixed derivative of total order<=j-1 of e_j R^j theta(R/epsilon_j) is bounded by2^-j, using epsilon_j^(j-k) and bounded coefficient derivatives on a fixed compact parameter set. Also require geometric decrease. Each fixed derivative series has a uniformly convergent tail. Repeated fundamental theorem identifies the sums as derivatives, including at the boundary. Because theta equals one near zero, only j=k contributes to the k-th normal derivative at zero, with value k! e_k and the corresponding parameter derivatives. Matching jets and the coordinate-segment fundamental theorem prove joint smoothness of the glued extension. The construction is local and retains full smooth parameter scope.

proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: The root average is even in rho, and the root difference divided by2rho equals the integral of q_s over[-1,1]/2, so both extend smoothly in R at zero and then across zero. Integrate the simplex q_ss formula first in v and then t to obtain exactly C10 at distinct nodes; multiplying the two fractions verifies C9. Continuity extends the identity to all repeated nodes. The substitution v->1-t-v proves evenness in rho, and the even-function theorem makes the full quotient jointly smooth in z,s,R>=0. The simplex has area one half, giving mu(z,0,0)=q_ss(z,0)/2 without any residual root-separation denominator.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every smooth scalar q with arbitrary smooth parameters, both signs of R including the joint corner s=R=0, all mixed derivatives and smooth substitutions R=R(z); no uniqueness claim for the negative-R extension.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For R<0 the denominator s²-R is positive. Telescoping divides each even and odd Taylor monomial, giving the exact polynomial quotient M_J and coefficients A_J,B_J. Their jets agree with a,b through order J, so integral Taylor remainders have the exact R^(J+1) factors and the q remainder has s^(2J+2). Set delta²=s²+|R|. The added induction represents each differentiated reciprocal as a sum C s^a(s²-R)^(-b) with2b-a=2+k+2l; |s|<=delta proves the full derivative bound. Product differentiation gives C16 for all k+2l<=2J and parameter derivatives. On R>=0 the simplex formula applied to the Taylor remainder, followed by the repeated even integral operation, gives the same bound. For any ordinary order K choose J>K+1; every remainder derivative through K tends to zero uniformly in the parameters. Extra quotient monomials have ordinary degree at least J, so the polynomial jets are consistent. Away from s=0 the denominator is nonzero and jets match directly; at the corner the coordinate-segment fundamental theorem identifies all extended derivatives. This proves the full smooth identity C17 across both signs.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: The flat decreasing cutoff, every derivative order and0<gamma<1 on bounded intervals, real phases phi0-cs with c>0 and epsilon>0, and fixed glancing neighborhoods including their negative-R portions.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Each negative-side derivative of chi is an exponential times a polynomial in1/v; the exponential series proves all polynomially weighted limits vanish at zero. The same argument treats sqrt(chi), sqrt(-chi prime) and the fractional-power derivative bounds C19. For p=s²+a0, R=-a0 and q=chi(phi0-cs-epsilon), q_s=-c chi prime>=0; the divided integral gives b>=0 on real roots. At the retained glancing point b=-c chi prime(-epsilon)>0. Continuity supplies a fixed positive neighborhood including R<0, without claiming arbitrary elliptic extensions are globally positive. At strict diffraction phi0=0 yields H_p phi=c partial_x a0<0 and hence positive H_p q. Multiply exact division by zeta² and differentiate; H_p p=0 gives all three terms of C23, including the outer-cutoff derivative and the equation multiple. The identity is at principal-symbol level and is not asserted to be an exact operator equation.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Compact tangential phase cutoffs with normal support allowed to meet the wall, all smooth scalar self-adjoint wave lower terms, and smooth Dirichlet inputs vanishing near the outer normal endpoint.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: On a neighborhood with b strictly positive, zeta sqrt(b) extends smoothly by zero because the support is strictly contained there. Finite products and adjoints give B=S* S principal symbol zeta²b and the real symmetrized A0 principal symbol zeta²a, including uniform normal derivatives. Thus the multiplier has at most one normal derivative and all lower terms retained. The exact earlier Green identity gives C25, with the nonnegative square ||S(0)d_xu(0)||² and actual forcing. Positivity follows from the operator square itself. Expanding d_xB=Bd_x-ihBprime and using uniform tangential bounds proves C26 with h<=1.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: The full exact interior commutator form for smooth and H2 Dirichlet inputs with compact normal support, actual f=P_hu inL2 and all lower terms; the original source data may have arbitrary compact interior distributional order.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Expand D8 and integrate its normal terms. The A0prime pair gives twice the real cross term; dBprime d gives its quadratic derivative form; the symmetrized remaining second derivatives give Re(Bprime d²u,u). Substitute d²u=f-Ru to retain both Re(Bprime f,u) and the R term. Self-adjointness of i[R,B]/h combines the two first-normal commutator terms; the final pair is -Re(BRprime u,u). All boundary terms vanish by u(0)=0. Finite differential-cutoff products and adjoints show R S,S R and their normal derivatives are bounded, [R,S]=O(h), and the product rule gives the same for B,A0. Each coefficient in the exact form is therefore uniformly bounded; Cauchy-Schwarz and2XY<=X²+Y² give C28. Odd reflection of an H2 zero-trace input has no normal delta terms; even normal and tangential mollification converge in H2 and preserve Dirichlet data. The primitive trace estimate gives normal-trace convergence and bounded smooth coefficients give convergence of P_hu. All terms thus pass to H2 inputs. The exact earlier inverse-power wave regularization supplies this finite regularity for arbitrary compact interior distributional data; no restriction of the source datum toH2 is imposed.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Full smooth formally self-adjoint scalar normal-gauged operators P_h=d_x²+R_h with all a0+ha1 differential terms, fixed compact tangential multiplier support, bounded required coefficient derivatives and a glancing point at which t0 is strictly positive.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Regroup the exact C27 form into self-adjoint T0,T1,T2, retaining Re(Bprime F,v). The symmetrized R products have scalar principal parts -a0 beta_x and -beta a0_x. Expand the adjoint and S*S product through the first correction with h² remainder; compact-frequency two-position amplitudes and their R compositions are bounded by kernel differentiation. Differential-cutoff products give (i/h)[R,Op a]=Op{a0,a}_tan+O(h), including all lower terms ha1. The h correction also contributes O(h), and h²E contributes O(h) because both R E and E R are bounded. Thus no h*O(1) remainder is divided by h without a commutator estimate. At a0=0 and s=0, H_p(alpha+s beta) equals {a0,alpha}_tan-beta a0_x=t0. The earlier signed phase identity supplies positivity only when its strict inequality holds; no incoming phase is presumed at every contact.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Fixed outer multiplier and positive c, arbitrary retained smooth coefficient bounds; normal-independent compact cutoffs q,theta with0<=q,theta<=1, and h chosen only after all cutoff derivatives are fixed.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Fix the outer operator norm K before choosing m with K sqrt(3m)+3Km<=c. Continuity at a0=0 supplies ell and nested q,theta so t0>=6c on q and |a0|<=m/2 on theta. The exact earlier cutoff construction supplies the cutoffs. Finite products give Q*T0Q=Op(t0 q²)+O(h) and Q*Q=Op(q²)+O(h). Positive packet quantization of (t0-4c)q² gives L10. With E=Op(theta(a0+ha1)), the scalar leading-constant norm bound gives ||E||<=m/2+Ctheta h<=m. The full separated-symbol calculus gives (R-E)Q=O(h^J), including differentiated compact-frequency remainders; hence L11. No smallness is inferred from an operator constant depending on the as-yet-unselected inner derivatives.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Distributional P_hu=f with u,d_xu,f in L2 and support before ell, zero localized Dirichlet trace, arbitrary nonzero forcing and the actual positive weighted boundary trace S_h(0)d_xQ_hu(0).
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Set v=Qu and F=Qf+[R,Q]u. Bounded Q R with tangential smoothing gives all needed fixed-h tangential derivatives and d_x²v inL2. The proved Hilbert primitive and odd-reflection approximation justify both traces and the exact Green form. Dirichlet energy gives Y²<=ZX+mX²+C_J h^J U X; two Young inequalities give L14 and its square-root L15. Insert these into4cX²-ChU²-KXY-KY²-KZX. The leading bad coefficient is at most c by the previously fixed choice of m; the remaining mixed terms absorb another c X² and leave CZ²+C_Jh^(2J)U². J=1 gives L17. The Bprime F term is included in KZX. The exact positive boundary identity is bounded by Ch^-1 Z(X+Y). Substituting L15, absorbing cX² and bounding h^-1 Z² and ZU yields L18 together with L14. The boundary norm stays weighted; no global inverse of S is asserted.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: All fixed finite remainder orders J, full scalar tangential differential symbol a0+ha1, nested compact q,g and an edge cutoff equal to one near the closed support of every positive derivative of q, uniformly on the retained normal interval.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: For QG, qg=q and every differentiated product meets derivatives of q and g at one point, hence vanishes; the full compact-frequency remainder is O(h^(J+1)) even after composing R on either side. For QR, transpose each c(y)eta^beta to obtain q times the finite sum binom(beta,gamma) eta^(beta-gamma)(ih)^|gamma| c^(gamma)(z). Taylor and frequency integration by parts contribute (-ih)^|delta|. Fix nu=gamma+delta and kappa derivatives on q; put mu=nu-kappa. If mu is not componentwise <=beta, the monomial derivative is zero. Otherwise its common coefficient times sum_gamma<=mu (-1)^|gamma|/[gamma!(mu-gamma)!] vanishes unless mu=0, by the finite binomial formula. The surviving coefficient is exactly (h/i)^|nu| eta^beta q_eta^nu c_y^nu/nu!. Taylor integral remainders are h^N compact-frequency bounded amplitudes, with normal derivatives controlled. Combining both products cancels the scalar zeroth term; every remaining symbol has a positive q derivative. Multiplication by the edge cutoff therefore changes it only by an arbitrarily high remainder. Together with [R,Q]=O(h), this proves all of L20, including lower differential terms and unlocalized tails.

proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Every H2 Dirichlet w on the collar, real normal cutoff psi equal to one at the wall and supported before ell, all retained scalar lower terms and arbitrary P_hw; no zero-forcing or regular-edge assumption.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Apply L18 to u=G(psi w), so v=K(psi w). Normal-independent Q,G commute with d_x. Combining Q[R,G]+[R,Q]G yields [R,K], while the exact normal commutator is -2ih psi prime d_x-h² psi double prime. This proves L21 with its signs. The L20 edge expansion bounds the tangential commutator by C h||Eedge psi w|| plus C_J h^(J+1)||psi w||. Divide the squared forcing bound by h²: obtain the equation factor h^-2, the edge and first normal term with factor1, the second normal term with h² and tail h^(2J). The lower-regularity term from L18 is h||G psi w||²; only the rapid tail uses the unlocalized norm. This is exactly L22. All constants and weighted boundary traces keep their stated scope.

proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: All derivatives of the small-band nonnegative g=q_s are bounded by every power g^(1-gamma), using flat cutoff derivatives and a phase slope bounded away from zero. A maximum over[-r,r] persists on a length min(r,A^gamma/(2C)), yielding A^(1+gamma)<=C average uniformly down to r0. Repeated even integral differentiation controls all z,R derivatives of the average by powers arbitrarily close to1. Chain differentiation of its square root then vanishes at every zero; component-interval fundamental theorem proves actual smooth extension. Away from r0 the exact one-root square root supplies the rest. Extend the square root, not the signed coefficient, by convergent jet summation; square it and adjust the quotient by the flat sDelta/(s²-R). All mixed corner derivatives vanish by the denominator estimate. The smaller elliptic adjustment can be supported where the shifted root is strictly nonzero. proof_nodes.hypotheses_and_scope: Whole-weight bulk form, both real roots and elliptic completion, full nonzero equation forcing, unbounded normal-frequency quotient tail and every fixed finite remainder order.
proof_nodes.all_used_results_and_checks: Divide the positive square root and edge, retaining the equation multiple.
